title: Garage With Three Bay Sizes
statement:
A small garage has three kinds of bays: large, medium and small. You know how many of each it has. Build the gate controller.

  • Garage(large, medium, small) sets the number of free bays of each kind.
  • park(size) handles one arriving car. size is 1 for a large car, 2 for a medium car and 3 for a small car. If a free bay of exactly that kind exists, the car takes it and the method returns true. Otherwise it returns false.

A car only fits its own bay kind: a small car does not take a free large bay. Cars never leave.

Tests are written as a list of operations and their arguments; the first operation creates the garage. The expected output has one entry per operation (null for the constructor).

examples.why: The large and medium bays fill. There are no small bays, and the only large bay is already taken by the time the second large car arrives.
The medium car is refused even though two large bays are free: bays are not shared across sizes.

hints: What is the only thing you need to remember about each bay kind?
Keep one counter of free bays per kind. Indexing an array by size avoids three if-branches.
park: if the counter for that size is above zero, decrement it and return true; otherwise return false.

explain.intuition:
Bays of the same kind are interchangeable and cars never leave, so the whole state is three numbers: how many free bays of each kind remain. A car either takes one (counter down by one) or is turned away.

Storing the counters in an array indexed by size keeps the method a single lookup, the same way you would key a UI state object by an enum instead of writing a switch.
steps: In the constructor store free = [0, large, medium, small], so free[size] matches the size codes 1, 2, 3.
pitfalls: Letting a car fall back to a bigger bay. The rules say a car only fits its own kind.
Decrementing before checking, which lets a counter go negative and then refuses cars after a later bay was never really freed.
Mixing up the codes: 1 is the large car, 3 is the small one.

solutions.title: Three counters in an array
solutions.idea: Keep the number of free bays per size in an array indexed by the size code.

followups: Cars can now leave. Which method do you add, and what must it check?
A small car may use a medium or large bay when its own kind is full. In what order should it try them, and why?
